sub_graphs.title: Safe Block: Justified Checkpoint as Safe Head
sub_graphs.description: Models the runtime behavior of determining the safe block using the most recent justified checkpoint, providing reorg protection under honest majority assumptions.

nodes.label: Justified Checkpoint Available in Store
nodes.description: The fork choice store contains a justified_checkpoint with a root pointing to a finalized-or-justified beacon block.

nodes.label: Get Safe Beacon Block Root
nodes.description: Returns store.justified_checkpoint.root as the safe beacon block root. This is a stopgap implementation.

nodes.label: Safe Beacon Block Root Determined
nodes.description: The safe beacon block root has been identified from the justified checkpoint.

nodes.label: Get Safe Execution Block Hash
nodes.description: Retrieves the beacon block for the safe root, checks if epoch >= BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH, and returns the execution payload block_hash or empty Hash32.

nodes.label: Safe Execution Block Hash Returned
nodes.description: The safe execution layer block hash is available for Engine API consumers.

edges.label: Return justified root as safe root
Use safe root to find execution hash
Return execution block hash or empty

external_entities.name: Engine API Consumer (Execution Layer)
external_entities.description: The execution layer client that queries the safe block hash via the Engine API for its own fork choice.

sub_graphs.title: Safe Block: Epoch-Based Bellatrix Gate
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation logic that determines whether a safe beacon block can yield an execution layer block hash, gating on the Bellatrix fork epoch.

nodes.label: Safe Beacon Block Retrieved from Store
nodes.description: The beacon block corresponding to the safe root has been retrieved from the block store.

nodes.label: Check Block Epoch >= BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH
nodes.description: Compare the block's epoch against BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH to determine if execution payloads exist.

nodes.label: Block is Pre-Bellatrix (No Execution Payload)
nodes.description: The safe block predates Bellatrix; no execution payload exists, return Hash32().

nodes.label: Block is Post-Bellatrix (Has Execution Payload)
nodes.description: The safe block is at or after Bellatrix; execution payload block_hash is available.

ambiguities.text: The get_safe_beacon_block_root function 'is meant to be improved in the future' using the justified checkpoint as 'a stopgap'.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the current justified-checkpoint-based implementation is the authoritative behavior for all deployed versions. Future improvements are out of scope. This is an assumption.

ambiguities.text: Safe from reorganization under 'honest majority and certain network synchronicity assumptions' without specifying exact synchronicity bounds.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard Ethereum synchronicity model: messages delivered within a known bounded delay. The exact bound is protocol-version-specific. This is an assumption.

implicit_assumptions.description: The justified checkpoint in the store is accurate and was produced by an honest supermajority of validators.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the justified checkpoint is based on a dishonest supermajority attestation, the 'safe' block may actually be on a fork that gets reorganized, misleading execution layer clients.

implicit_assumptions.description: The beacon block store always contains the block referenced by the justified checkpoint root.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A missing block would cause get_safe_execution_block_hash to fail, potentially returning a stale or incorrect safe head to the execution layer.
